html:
Operation Condor was a secret alliance of the South American dictatorships, set up in Santiago in November 1975, to hunt and kill their opponents across borders.

Its members were Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia and Brazil. It was led by Manuel Contreras, head of the Chilean secret police under Pinochet. Exiles who had fled one dictatorship were seized in another and sent home or killed. Its agents also struck in the United States and Europe: in 1976 a car bomb in Washington killed the former Chilean minister Orlando Letelier.

The United States knew of the plan. Thousands of people were victims. The discovery of the Archives of Terror in Paraguay in 1992 exposed much of it, and courts in Argentina convicted leaders of the operation in 2016. It shows how the Cold War joined the dictatorships of the south in Chile and beyond.
sum: Operation Condor was a secret alliance of the South American dictatorships, set up in Santiago in November 1975, to hunt and kill their opponents across borders.
